title: Edward Lee (and Ghinucci) to Wolsey from Spain, 1526-1529 (BL Cotton MS Vespasian C III-C IV; DECODE R8458-R8587)

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C IV (DECODE R8566)

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment written above each of the four cipher runs.

transcription.notes: Only the interlinear decipherment was transcribed; the sign cipher was spot-checked, not transcribed.

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C III f. 238 (DECODE R8465)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the manuscript; printed deciphered in Letters and Papers Henry VIII iv no. 2097.

transcription.notes: Three cipher lines on f. 238v transcribed sign by sign; two or three signs doubtful.

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C III f. 245 (DECODE R8472-R8473)

plaintext.source: Tuke's decipherment, image 4 of R8473; L&P iv 2173.

transcription.notes: Two cipher blocks read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key, checked against Tuke; plaintext word count by hand.

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C IV ff. 109-110 (DECODE R8533)

plaintext.source: Tuke's interlinear decipherment on f. 110r only; ff. 109r-v deciphered by Tuke from the 8 April original (TNA, not online). L&P iv 3028/3055.

transcription.notes: Three passes; cipher plaintext words counted by script from the token list; 414 read (90.6%).

system.summary: Lee-Worcester sign cipher (1526-29): graphic-sign alphabet with word and name signs.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key, document on DECODE R8566
system.notes: Cipher only in four short runs of R8566. The other DECODE records (R8458-R8460, R8462, R8536-R8538, R8542-R8544, R8549, R8550, R8561, R8585-R8587, and R8602 of 20 Apr 1529 R8578 of 16 Oct 1528 and R8547-R8548 of 29 June 1527, all added later) are clear despatches with no cipher, so they are not listed as documents.

prior_solution.where: Interlinear contemporary decipherment in R8566; Tomokiyo key on DECODE R8566

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded all 46 images of the 17 DECODE records and the key document on R8566 with the session cookie.
Looked at every page: 16 records are clear despatches to Wolsey with no cipher; R8566 has four short cipher runs.
Transcribed the contemporary interlinear decipherment of the four runs in R8566.
Spot-checked against Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key: signs under 'possibilite ... good' read p-o-ss-i-b-i-l-i-t-e and g-o-o-d.
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8602 (catalogue 104, Cotton Vesp. C IV f. 341, 20 Apr 1529) with the session cookie.
Looked at both pages: a clear English despatch of Lee to Wolsey dated at Saragossa 20 April 1529, with postscript and signature; no cipher.
Catalogue 106 (DECODE R8578, Vesp. C IV f. 284, 16 Oct 1528, 'Epus Wigorn, Ed. Lee'): downloaded both images with the session cookie.
Looked at both pages of R8578: a clear English despatch of Ghinucci and Lee to Wolsey, Valladolid 16 Oct 1528, on English ships seized by the Emperor's subjects; no cipher sign on either page.
Read the full clear text of R8578 (both pages) into r8578_reading.txt.
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8582 (catalogue 105, Vesp. C IV f. 300/old 276, 18 Nov 1528).
Applied Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key to R8582: 'worde for worde', 'erle of Desmonte' read; a full cipher page, no interlinear decipherment.
Letters and Papers IV no. 4948 calendars R8582 as cipher with 'Decipher of the above by Tuke' at f. 276*; summary agrees (earl of Desmond's courier).
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8465 (catalogue 102) and its key document with the session cookie.
Transcribed the three cipher lines on f. 238v sign by sign.
Applied Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key (DOC_8465): 'thynke yf your grace speke somme thynge herof to the Emperoris ambassador ... come I thynke they wolde be gladde to see your grace contente'.
Letters and Papers iv no. 2097 (BHO) prints the same passage deciphered in italics; the reading agrees.
Catalogue 116 (DECODE R8547-R8548, Vesp. C IV ff. 139-140, 29 June 1527, 'Ed. Lee Almosinar'): downloaded all four images with the session cookie.
Looked at all four pages: one clear English despatch of Lee to Wolsey, Valladolid 29 June 1527 ('your grace most bounden priest'), split across the two records; no cipher sign on any page.
Catalogue 109 (DECODE R8552-R8555, R8568, R8573, Vesp. C IV, 1527, 'Eps. Wigorn'): downloaded all 18 images with the session cookie; contact sheet.
R8552-R8555 are clear leaves of L&P IV 3271 (17 July 1527); R8568 has its cipher runs deciphered interlinearly.

R8573 (Burgos, MS dated 26 Dec 1527) is a real cipher letter with no gloss; matched to L&P IV 3518 through its ciphered postscript's clear gloss ('not yet spoken of the French king's cession of the title of Milan'); L&P records Tuke's 5-page decipherment and misdates the letter 26 Oct.
Downloaded the two images of DECODE R8559 (catalogue 112, Vesp. C IV f. 164/old 152, July 1527) and Tomokiyo's key document on the record.

Applied Tomokiyo's Lee-Worcester key to the one cipher run on p. 2 of R8559: the '-mation' letters fit the interlinear gloss 'but the intimation'; rest of both pages clear English, p. 1 signs are reference marks.
Downloaded the eight images of DECODE R8575 (catalogue 107, Vesp. C IV ff. 262-265/old 243-244, 28 July 1528).

Letters and Papers IV no. 4564 calendars R8575 as 'Mostly cipher, pp. 7' with '2. Decipher by Tuke. Pp. 7' at f. 245; the clear passages on p. 1 (Radcliff, the ship taken in Bayonna in Galicia) match the summary word for word.
Catalogue 101: downloaded the 13 images of R8472, R8473, R8533, R8535 and Tomokiyo's key documents with the session cookie.
R8472 and R8535 clear; R8473 f. 245 and R8533 ff. 109-110 carry the Lee-Worcester sign cipher.
L&P iv 2173 (13 May 1526, deciphered by Tuke), 3055 (20 Apr 1527 duplicate of 3028, 8 Apr, Tuke's decipher at R.O.).
R8473 read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key; then found Tuke's decipherment is image 4 of the record; agrees word for word.
R8533 first pass with Tomokiyo's key: about 83% (estimated).
Used L&P iv 3028's quotations of the 8 April original as a crib for R8533: 85.7% then 86.4% counted.
Third pass: ÷ with bar = them, Ⱶ = the Emperor, # = would, the 'marquis' group = INACHUS; 414/457 (90.6%). Name signs and underlined clusters stay open.

outcome.notes: Read at the time; 16 of 17 records carry no cipher. Nothing new to read. R8602 (catalogue 104, 1529) is the same: clear, no cipher. R8578 (catalogue 106, 16 Oct 1528) is the same: clear, no cipher. R8582 (catalogue 105, 18 Nov 1528) is a full cipher page, read at the time by Tuke (L&P IV 4948 ii). R8559 (catalogue 112, July 1527) is clear with one short cipher run deciphered interlinearly ('but the intimation'); part of L&P IV 3271. Catalogue 101: R8472-73 (13 May 1526, to Henry VIII) read at the time by Tuke (image 4), re-read, agrees; R8535 clear; R8533 (20 Apr 1527 duplicate) read at the time from the original (Tuke, TNA), re-read here 90.6% with the L&P crib.
